Magnets and materials

Ray: On to the machine learning for materials desk. First, a small data story. Spin crossover metal organic frameworks are porous molecular materials that can switch spin state. The abstract says only a small number of active ones are known among thousands already synthesized.

Ray: A random forest trained on those two hundred recovers eighty two percent of true positives, with only two false negatives. They then applied it to the unlabeled set and got a new collection of high confidence candidates called p S C O one oh five.

Experimental evidence reported for p-wave magnetism in europium silicide

Phys.org · Quantum physics · 7/10

Phys.org reports that an international team found compelling experimental evidence for p-wave magnetism in EuSi, a chemically simple metal. P-wave magnetism is an unconventional kind of magnetic order, so finding it in a simple rare-earth compound would be notable. The excerpt gives no measurement details, so how strong the evidence is remains open.

Quantile active learning finds spin-crossover MOFs from 200 noisy labels

npj Computational Materials · 5/10

The abstract reports a quantile-regression-tree active-learning strategy that chose 200 metal-organic frameworks for electronic-structure evaluation despite noisy labels from unrelaxed geometries. A random forest trained on those labels recovers 82% of true positives, with two false negatives. Spin crossover is a spin-state switching behavior in some molecular materials, not ferromagnetism, but the small-data selection idea could carry over to other searches.

Analysis: US minerals push has not yet loosened China's grip

News · rare earths & magnets policy · 7/10

WTVB publishes an analysis, ahead of Xi talks, asking whether US minerals policy has reduced dependence on China for rare earths. Only the headline was available, so the evidence behind the conclusion is unconfirmed. It adds to the wider debate over rare-earth supply chains that matter for magnets.

China's magnet exports to US and EU fall after September rebound

News · rare earths & magnets policy · 6/10

The South China Morning Post reports that rare-earth magnet exports to the US and EU dropped in October after rebounding in September. Agenzia Nova adds that Japan bucked the trend. Only headlines were available, so the size of the changes is unconfirmed, but the swings illustrate how volatile magnet supply can be.

Odd-parity f-wave magnons emerge from topological excitons in Haldane-Hubbard model

Physical Review Letters · 6/10

The abstract reports that topological excitons soften and condense into a Néel state, where they become Goldstone magnons with f-wave spin splitting. It also states that closing an electronic band gap forces a magnon band gap to close. This is a theory paper with no specific material, so its applications remain conceptual for now.

ML · Magnetic Materials

Hematite magnon splitting calculated from first principles, g-wave to i-wave

arXiv · ML materials discovery · 5/10

The abstract reports fully relativistic ab initio calculations of altermagnetic and anisotropic magnon splitting and lifetimes in hematite, an iron oxide. It also reports a transition to i-wave symmetry in the kz=0 plane. Magnons are quantized spin waves, and this is a first-principles theory result that includes spin-orbit effects and anisotropy.

Octupolar magneto-optics proposed for altermagnets such as CrSb and RuO2

arXiv · ML materials discovery · 5/10

The abstract says octupolar magneto-optical effects can arise without net magnetization and may not require spin-orbit coupling. Calculations show microradian-scale Faraday rotation in a 100-nm sample, with the sign reversing between magnetic domains. That could offer a route to imaging domains in altermagnets, but so far it is a numerical prediction awaiting experimental confirmation.

Review: efficient ML interatomic potentials unified through Atomic Cluster Expansion

arXiv · ML materials discovery · 5/10

The abstract frames many machine-learned interatomic potential architectures as variants of one underlying framework, the Atomic Cluster Expansion. It reports that on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, three- to five-layer models approach the accuracy of deeper ones. The abstract does not say whether the comparison extends to magnetic systems.

Path-probability theory of the East model compared with Monte Carlo

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 5/10

The abstract reports closed equations for a one-dimensional kinetic Ising model, the East model, that agree closely with Monte Carlo simulations over a wide temperature range. The theory does not capture the exact low-temperature super-Arrhenius scaling. It is a case study in checking an analytic theory against simulation.

Graph attention network predicts LPBF part distortion from STL geometry

arXiv · ML for manufacturing · 3/10

The abstract reports an R² of 0.946 on 117 parts, using five-fold cross-validation split by part and labels from ANSYS simulations. Because the labels are simulated rather than measured, this is a surrogate model for distortion in laser powder bed fusion, not a monitoring method. The available text does not say whether measured distortion data back it up.

AMCM links EOSPRINT build data to PanX thermomechanical simulation

3D Printing Industry · 5/10

3D Printing Industry reports an integration that moves build data into a thermomechanical simulation and writes optimized process information back. It is a simulation-first workflow in which predictions inform the build. It is vendor news, so independent validation is not yet confirmed.

Theoretical Physics

Symmetry-resolved errors in tensor-network RG at six-vertex criticality

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 6/10

The abstract reports that, for loop tensor network renormalization on the c=1 critical line, the dominant truncation error is a dimerization operator. Its growth per renormalization step agrees with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. A larger bond dimension lowers the error's amplitude but not its type or growth rate, which matters for trusting numerics near criticality.

Exact decay length derived for the sign-alternating kagome Ising model

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 6/10

The abstract gives a closed-form fermionic decay length that diverges on two classical critical branches. In a scaling limit, those branches become gap-closing conditions of a transverse-field Ising chain, and the decay length approaches the localization length of a Majorana end mode. The result links classical Ising criticality to transverse-field Ising physics and is an exact analytic result.

Bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere data probe whether the SO(5) deconfined critical point is real

arXiv · statistical mechanics · 6/10

A deconfined critical point is a proposed continuous transition between two magnetic orders, which standard theory would expect to be abrupt, first-order. The open question is whether it is a true scale-invariant point or only a near-miss that drifts slowly. The abstract reports a bootstrap cone whose tip lies close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC, plus agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, which uses exact diagonalization up to N=12.

Lattice evidence that light fermion masses can trigger the Higgs effect

arXiv · high-energy theory · 6/10

The Higgs mechanism gives Standard Model particles their mass, but what triggers it remains an open question. The abstract reports lattice simulations without Yukawa couplings in which light fermion masses appear to trigger the Higgs effect. The transition occurs when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass, and the system studied is an SU(2) toy model rather than the full Standard Model.
